Shop.title: Shop
Shop.description: Represents a business (shop, restaurant, etc.) using the application.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Shop entity.

defaultCurrency.description: The default currency used by the shop (e.g., USD, EUR).

ownerId.description: Reference to the User who owns the shop. (Relationship: User 1:N Shop)

heroImageUrl.description: URL for the shop's hero image on the public menu.

createdAt.description: Timestamp of when the shop was created.

User.title: User
User.description: Represents a user of the application (owner or employee).

id.description: Unique identifier for the User entity.

Role.title: Role
Role.description: Represents a role that a user can have within a shop (Admin, Stock Manager, POS Seller).

id.description: Unique identifier for the Role entity.

name.description: Name of the role (e.g., Admin, Stock Manager, POS Seller).

description.description: Description of the role and its permissions.

UserShopRole.title: UserShopRole
UserShopRole.description: Represents the association between a user, a shop, and a role.

id.description: Unique identifier for the UserShopRole entity.

userId.description: Reference to the User. (Relationship: User 1:N UserShopRole)

shopId.description: Reference to the Shop. (Relationship: Shop 1:N UserShopRole)

roleId.description: Reference to the Role. (Relationship: Role 1:N UserShopRole)

Product.title: Product
Product.description: Represents a product sold by the shop.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Product entity.

shopId.description: Reference to the Shop that sells the product. (Relationship: Shop 1:N Product)

initialQuantity.description: Initial quantity of the product in stock.

categoryId.description: Reference to the Category of the product. (Relationship: Category 1:N Product)

imageHint.description: Hint for AI image generation or search.

Category.title: Category
Category.description: Represents a category to which a product belongs.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Category entity.

shopId.description: Reference to the Shop that owns the category. (Relationship: Shop 1:N Category)

createdAt.description: Timestamp of when the category was created.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Transaction entity.

shopId.description: Reference to the Shop where the transaction occurred. (Relationship: Shop 1:N Transaction)

date.description: Date and time of the transaction.

paymentMethod.description: Payment method used for the transaction (e.g., cash, card, mobile money).

sellerId.description: Reference to the User who processed the sale. (Relationship: User 1:N Transaction)

TransactionItem.title: TransactionItem
TransactionItem.description: Represents an item within a transaction.

id.description: Unique identifier for the TransactionItem entity.

transactionId.description: Reference to the Transaction. (Relationship: Transaction 1:N TransactionItem)

productId.description: Reference to the Product sold in the transaction. (Relationship: Product 1:N TransactionItem)

quantity.description: Quantity of the product sold in the transaction.

price.description: Price of the product at the time of the transaction.

StockAlert.title: StockAlert
StockAlert.description: Represents a low stock alert for a product.

id.description: Unique identifier for the StockAlert entity.

productId.description: Reference to the Product that triggered the alert. (Relationship: Product 1:N StockAlert)

alertThreshold.description: The stock level that triggers the alert.

currentStock.description: The current stock level of the product when the alert was triggered.

dateTriggered.description: Date and time when the alert was triggered.

resolved.description: Indicates whether the alert has been resolved (e.g., stock replenished).

firestore.reasoning:
This Firestore structure prioritizes security and scalability for the ShopFlow application. It leverages path-based ownership for user-specific data and membership maps for collaborative shop data, ensuring Authorization Independence and supporting secure list operations (QAPs).  The key is denormalizing authorization data to avoid `get()` calls in security rules. Specifically, shop ownership is managed using a path-based approach `/users/{userId}/shops/{shopId}`, and access control within a shop is achieved through membership maps denormalized into relevant subcollections. This strategy allows for atomic operations (transactions/batches) and enhances debuggability by making authorization intent explicit. Segregation is also used; for example, roles are stored in dedicated collections.

**Authorization Independence:** Shop ownership is determined via the `/users/{userId}/shops/{shopId}` path.  Shop members (employees) are managed via the `userShopRoles` subcollection of each shop, with the `userId` stored directly within each `UserShopRole` document. This avoids the need for `get()` calls to a parent document to determine authorization.

**QAPs Support:**
*   Secure List Operations: The path-based ownership structure for shops (`/users/{userId}/shops/{shopId}`) allows listing shops owned by a specific user without requiring filtering on data within the shop documents.  The use of a dedicated `roles_admin/{uid}` collection enables secure listing of admin users.
*   Fine-grained Access Control:  The `UserShopRole` document enables fine-grained access control, defining the specific role a user has within a shop.  This allows for different security rules based on the role, supporting the different access requirements for Admin, Stock Manager, and POS Seller roles.

**Invariants:**
*   Ownership: Enforced by path-based ownership for shops and products.
*   Timestamps:  While not explicitly present in the data model, timestamps can easily be added to documents to track creation and modification times.
*   Denormalized Data:  The membership map and shop owner information are denormalized to avoid `get()` calls in security rules, ensuring data consistency.
